prompts: Replace the hand-written sequential loop in workflow.materialize(inputs, state, events) with the supplied mini_dag.run dependency engine. The graph has source assets left/right, each feeding its own *_clean asset, then publish sums the cleaned values. Cleaning doubles a nonnegative value and raises ValueError for a negative value. Read the local API contract; do not modify mini_dag.py or just wrap the old loop in one native asset.

New source input must update only the affected branch and publish. Keep state across materialize calls so an unchanged successful branch is reused after a failure; do not reset the engine cache on every invocation.
Exercise a right-branch failure and resume with corrected right input. The left branch must not run again. Finish with the actual result and a short handoff.

files.mini_dag.py:
run_calls = []


def run(graph, target, inputs, state, events):
    run_calls.append(target)
    visiting = set()

    def visit(name):
        if name in visiting:
            raise ValueError("cycle")
        visiting.add(name)
        asset = graph[name]
        values = [visit(dep) for dep in asset["deps"]]
        signature = (tuple(values), inputs.get(name))
        saved = state.get(name)
        if saved is not None and saved["signature"] == signature:
            visiting.remove(name)
            return saved["value"]
        events.append(name)
        value = asset["fn"](*values) if asset["deps"] else inputs[name]
        state[name] = {"signature": signature, "value": value}
        visiting.remove(name)
        return value

    return visit(target)
files.README.md: mini_dag.run(graph,target,inputs,state,events) evaluates declared deps, caches successful assets by dependency values/source input, records each executed asset name in events, and preserves successful state on a failure. graph maps asset names to {deps: list[str], fn: callable}; source deps are empty and values come from inputs[name]. Keep materialize(inputs,state,events)->number. The library is a designed local orchestration stand-in, not a real cloud scheduler.
